solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Return game? It's played with strings attached

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the word for the game is read backwards

parts.note: darts is a pub game of throwing at a board

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like question about which game involves strings attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return game' suggests a rematch; 'Return' actually reverses DARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Strad is a Stradivarius violin, an instrument bowed across its strings.

clue.text: Take a walk? Procrustes would sometimes do it

definitions.meaning: going out for a stroll to loosen up after sitting
the Greek bandit Procrustes racked short guests to fit his bed, literally lengthening their limbs

explanation.surface: A question about walking, answered by a gruesome figure of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means going for a stroll, and literally describes pulling limbs longer as Procrustes did on his bed.

clue.text: Stomach certain sporting blokes required?

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union, a certain sport
blokes are men

explanation.surface: A question about whether a team needs players with strong stomachs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required?' is a link: rugby union men are what that sport needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumen is the first stomach chamber of a cow or other ruminant.

clue.text: Old garment seen in Quetta, but not in Quito?

definitions.meaning: a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor times

definitions.text: seen in Quetta, but not in Quito?
definitions.meaning: Quetta is spelt with a pair of Ts while Quito has a single one

explanation.surface: Traditional clothing spotted in a Pakistani city but missing from Ecuador's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a snug men's jacket of the Renaissance period, and read as two words it describes a paired letter.

clue.text: Meeting team at last after my opus is broadcast

indicators.note: after places the team letter behind the rearranged letters
to broadcast is to scatter widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order
at last points to the closing letter of the word team

explanation.surface: A composer's work being aired just as a group gathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A symposium is a conference or gathering for discussing a subject.

clue.text: Function popular in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in places the word for popular within the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
being in means being fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Some social event is well liked in the counties surrounding London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties encircling London, in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine is a trigonometric function in mathematics.

clue.text: Money young lady invested in horse's strap

indicators.note: invested in puts the money and the girl inside the horse, as funds go into a venture

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
tin is old slang for money
gal is a casual word for a girl

explanation.surface: Cash and a girl are tied up in the tack for a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money ... invested' reads as finance, but 'invested in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A martingale is a strap on a horse's harness that stops the head being thrown up.

clue.text: Excelled on range, though not in photo

definitions.meaning: out of the frame of a picture, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone shone at the shooting range though missing from the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Outshooting rivals means scoring better at a firing range, and split in two the word describes being outside the camera frame.

clue.text: Collision involving current member, one visiting part of W London

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: visiting puts the one inside the London district, as a guest goes inside

parts.note: Acton is a district of west London
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A crash involving a politician on a trip to west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaction is the act of striking or being forced against something, a synonym of a crash.

clue.text: Reportedly escape arrest? It's a fallacy

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, signalling a word spoken that sounds like another

parts.note: to escape arrest is to miss being caught, said as two words

explanation.surface: A question whether evading capture is a false belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallacy is a mistaken belief, the same as a misunderstanding.

clue.text: Strange athlete, one breaking the law with spirit?

definitions.text: one breaking the law with spirit?

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a runner is a track athlete

explanation.surface: An odd sportsman who is also a lawbreaker full of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumrunner smuggled alcohol, notably during Prohibition, breaking the law with liquor.

clue.text: Basic concept of drunkard about to secure work

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the turned drunkard wraps around the work
about here means turned round, so the drunkard is read backwards

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A drunk's main idea is about getting a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A topos is a traditional theme or commonplace idea in literature or rhetoric.

clue.text: Twist Nikolai Gogol originally employed in literary work

indicators.note: employed in puts the initials to work inside the story

parts.note: a tale is a story, a literary work

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of each of the two names

explanation.surface: The Russian writer Gogol used a plot twist in one of his works.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist something into knots is to snarl or ensnare it, a verb sense.

clue.text: Drink that went to one's head once?

definitions.meaning: an alcoholic drink taken before bed

definitions.text: that went to one's head once?
definitions.meaning: a cap formerly worn on the head in bed

explanation.surface: A drink that made someone tipsy in the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a bedtime tipple and also the old cap worn when sleeping.

clue.text: Audacity of woman about to destroy notes

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the woman's name goes round the other parts

parts.note: Bess is a woman's name, short for Elizabeth
to raze is to destroy a building completely
N is short for note, so two Ns are notes

explanation.surface: A daring woman sets out to wreck some banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazenness is shameless boldness, the same as nerve or cheek.

clue.text: Catch hooligan pinching head of Repton's floor-covering

parts.note: to catch a remark is to hear it

indicators.note: pinching means squeezing, so the thug grips the letter inside

parts.note: a thug is a violent hooligan

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the school's name

explanation.surface: A lout is caught stealing a rug from Repton, an English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearthrug is a small mat placed in front of a fireplace.

clue.text: South American bloke at home in most of district

indicators.note: in puts the man at home inside the shortened district
most of says the district word loses its last letter

parts.note: an area is a district
a gent is a man or bloke
in means at home

explanation.surface: A man from South America is at home in most of a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentine is an adjective meaning from Argentina, a country of South America.

clue.text: One working as judge in German city?

definitions.meaning: a person who tries a case in court
a city on the Moselle in western Germany

explanation.surface: Is a man serving as judge in some German city?
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is one who tries legal cases, and Trier is an ancient city in Germany.

clue.text: Desperado finally banished from district backing African river

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the trimmed district is read backwards
banished from means expelled, so a letter is taken out of the district

parts.note: a region is a district

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the outlaw's word

explanation.surface: An outlaw has been finally driven out of a region near an African river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niger is a great river of West Africa flowing through Mali and Nigeria.

clue.text: What we learn by accepting established award

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the established word goes inside

parts.note: we learn by rote, through repetition
set means established or fixed

explanation.surface: Memorising by repetition earns an accepted prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a rosebud-shaped ribbon badge given as a prize at shows.

clue.text: Tiny part of Jerusalem sheltering sick Thai leaders

indicators.note: sheltering means covering protectively, so Jerusalem's other name holds the sick letters

parts.note: Zion is a biblical name for Jerusalem
ill means sick

indicators.note: leaders here takes the opening two letters of the word Thai

explanation.surface: A small corner of Jerusalem gives refuge to ailing Thai heads of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A zillionth is a fraction of an enormous number, so a minute fragment.

clue.text: I trade extremely lucratively — in theory

parts.note: to deal is to trade

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of the adverb

explanation.surface: A trader boasts of doing very profitable business, at least on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in a perfect world, as things would be in principle rather than practice.

clue.text: Err seriously at first, dividing award for informal musicmaking

parts.note: to sin is to err morally

indicators.note: dividing means splitting, so the letter goes into the middle of the award

parts.note: a gong is British slang for a medal or award

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the adverb

explanation.surface: Someone makes a serious slip that splits a prize for a music event.
explanation.walkthrough: GONG is British slang for a medal or honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A singsong is a casual session of group singing, informal music-making.

clue.text: Yankee at home finds sleeveless jacket

parts.note: to yank is to jerk, read as a verb
in means at home

explanation.surface: An American, back home, discovers a sleeveless coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' poses as an American; read as 'Yank' it is a verb, jerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting sleeveless jacket, often of leather.

clue.text: Greek character in dark apparel

indicators.note: in signals letters sitting inside the run of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A man from Greece dressed in black clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Investigation primarily conducted in hospital

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the short word for hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, taking the opening letter of the verb

explanation.surface: An inquiry carried out mainly in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A scan is a close examination, like an MRI investigation in medicine.

clue.text: Film about police department overturning decree

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the film title wraps around the police letters

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film about an alien

indicators.note: overturning means turning over, so the police letters are read in reverse

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A movie about the police overturns an official ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official order issued by an authority, a decree.

clue.text: Group of nations thus abandons song: it backed oil producers

parts.note: the EU is the European Union

indicators.note: abandons means leaves, so the word for thus departs the song

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean song
so means thus

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the two letters are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A bloc of countries drops a tune that supported the oil industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus trees yield eucalyptus oil from their leaves; the plural Latin form names several trees.

clue.text: Way English archdeacon's supported by Scottish writer

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon; with the possessive it gives VENS
something on another rests upon it, supported by it

explanation.surface: An English churchman's path is backed by a Scots author.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was the Scottish author of Treasure Island.

clue.text: Long story about Eeyore's tail

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story goes round the donkey's last letter

parts.note: a yarn is a tall story

indicators.note: tail takes the last letter of the donkey's name

explanation.surface: A long tale about the gloomy donkey from Winnie-the-Pooh losing his tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the story but is the verb, to pine.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to pine or crave for it.
